pages.transcription:
27. I 1941 Dear H. a. Manfred, Lotte will write
you about Eva more in detail. Please do not
worry, we shall find the right thing. I personally
believe she should be somewhere, where there is
more discipline and also more continental atmos-
phere; perhaps because I am a writer that I attach
more importance to spontaneous writing {than others} and I was
not satisfied with Eva on this behalf - for instance
my sister in law did send her very nice Christmas
presents (also for the boy at Salinas) and she thanked
for it the 16th of January, three weeks later! There
must be someone who looks after her in all those
things of negligence which are every one trifling
but if they become a habit would affect her charac-
ter and be a big disadvantage in later life. I am
sorry we cannot take her with us when we are
going now to a little place {or town} because all is
too uncertain how long we shall stay there as it
will suit us there - I believe some boarding-school
would be the best and we will look round in the
next days to arrange all as well as we can
before we leave, which will be in any case not
before the first week-end in February. The weather
is here as bad as possible - what a contrast with
Rio! We hope you feel alright! Kindest regards
to all! Yours
StefanZweig
